html:
Kipchoge Keino is a Kenyan runner whose victory in the 1,500 metres at the 1968 Olympic Games in Mexico City, beating the American world record holder Jim Ryun, launched Kenya as a power in distance running.

A police officer from the Nandi hills, he ran despite a gallbladder illness and won by a wide margin at high altitude. He won gold in the steeplechase in 1972.

Kenyan runners, many of them Kalenjin from the highlands around Eldoret, have since dominated distance races, among them Eliud Kipchoge, who ran a marathon under two hours in 2019. Keino and his wife cared for hundreds of orphans on their farm. He later led Kenya's Olympic committee, a hero of Kenya like Wangari Maathai, and of the Olympic movement.
